tagline: How slicer filters travel through the data model via relationships

slides.title: How Filters Travel
slides.body: In a star schema, when a user selects a value in a slicer connected to a dimension table, that filter automatically flows to the fact table via the relationship — restricting which rows are visible in all measures.
slides.keyPoint: Filters travel from the ONE side (dimension) to the MANY side (fact) by default. This is single-direction cross-filtering.

slides.title: FactSales — All Rows (No Filter)
slides.caption: Without any slicer, all 4 rows are visible

slides.title: User Selects 'Bikes' in Category Slicer
slides.caption: Filter flows: DimCategory → FactSales via relationship

slides.title: Total Revenue with 'Bikes' Filter
steps: Filter propagates to FactSales via the relationship

slides.title: Bidirectional Filtering — Use With Caution
bullets: Single-direction (default): filter flows dimension → fact only. Safest for performance and RLS.
Bidirectional: filter flows both ways. Needed for some many-to-many or disconnected table scenarios.
Bidirectional can cause RLS bypass — filters propagating unexpectedly through the fact table can expose hidden data.
Bidirectional increases query plan complexity — VertiPaq must evaluate both filter directions.
slides.warning: Never use bidirectional cross-filtering by default. Enable it only when explicitly needed and verify that RLS filters still work correctly after enabling it.
